order_a_first.reason: B more closely reconstructs the target mechanism by linking increased ordering/APB energy to restricted cross-slip, planar slip, and stress concentration at phase boundaries, followed by ductility recovery when ordering weakens. Its cited evidence also more directly supports high APB energy in ordered precipitates and planar dislocation slip through coherent ordered domains. A instead emphasizes B2-domain coherence and an unsupported cross-slip-locking mechanism, with a less accurate temperature range. B remains imperfect: it incorrectly locates the critical ordering primarily in B2 rather than enhanced L12 order in FCC, omits jagged PB tips and ductile transition zones, gives only an approximate 500–700°C boundary rather than the <550/550–750/>750°C regime, and does not specify the decisive TKD/TEM observation of pile-ups and crack initiation at jagged PB tips with absent grain-boundary segregation.

order_b_first.reason: A is closer to the target mechanism because it links increased anti-phase-boundary energy to restricted cross-slip, planar slip, and stress concentration at phase boundaries, followed by recovery when ordering weakens. It also proposes direct TEM/APT tests and explicitly checks for absent impurity segregation. However, it incorrectly places the critical ordering in B2 rather than enhanced L12 order in FCC, omits jagged PB tips and ductile transition zones, and gives an inaccurate temperature window. B correctly identifies the as-cast AlCoCrFeNi2.1 FCC/B2 microstructure but likewise assigns ordering to B2, substitutes coherence loss for jagged-boundary evolution, gives a poorer temperature range, and does not specify the required PB-tip pile-up/crack-initiation measurement. Its cross-slip-locking claim is also less directly supported by its cited evidence.
